group: How much of each market is owned from abroad
title: How much of Colombia's debt securities is owned from abroad: non-residents and residents, in its own currency
short: Colombia debt securities, owned from abroad
source: OECD financial balance sheets, non-consolidated, quarterly (DSD_NASEC20@DF_T720R_Q), Colombia (COL): issued by residents (sector S1, liabilities) and held by non-residents (S2, assets), debt securities (F3), national currency; residents = issued minus non-residents (our calculation). note: Each book splits everything residents of Colombia have issued of debt securities into the part held by non-residents, as the country reports it to the OECD, and the rest, held by residents (our calculation: issued minus non-residents), in its own currency and at market value. Non-residents means every holder outside the country, including foreign central banks and funds. It does not say which kind of resident holds the rest, which needs the country's own accounts. Measured the other way, from residents' holdings of every issuer minus their foreign holdings, residents hold 4.5% of the total less than shown here, so Colombia's own figures do not fully agree with each other. Source: OECD.
